# Marathon Pace KM editorial audit

10 November 2026. Baseline: `f234794`. The audit covered 125 published pages and the 404 page. The review compared page introductions, headings, repeated blocks and navigation, with browser checks at 390 px and 1280 px and visual spot checks of the main layouts.

| Area | Finding | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage and navigation | A slogan, decorative labels and repeated tool descriptions competed with the pace chart. The training duration guide was hard to find. | Put the chart and calculator first, simplify the tool links and list the training duration guide first under Training on desktop and mobile. |
| Goal charts and calculators | Intros repeated what the controls and tables already showed. Repeated caveats delayed the useful numbers. | Open with the pace, split or input the runner needs. Keep rounding, assumptions and important limits with the result or methods. |
| Training, pacing and race guides | Long headings, boxes around ordinary paragraphs and explanations of the page itself made advice harder to scan. | Use shorter headings and a narrower reading column. Open with the answer, then show the example or worksheet. |
| Running Lab and About | Process descriptions overshadowed the race accounts. Several blocks repeated how the data should be read. | Lead with Davin's recorded splits, race notes and next steps. Keep the original charts and place the source and limit notes beside the relevant evidence. |
| Melbourne venues and guide index | Repeated card styling made the directory look busier than it needed to. | Use plain linked rows for the guides and quieter venue cards. Retain access, surface and location details. |
| Site information | The same brand and editorial explanations appeared in several places. | Use a shorter About page and one shared footer that links to methods, editorial policy and corrections. |

The visible copy is about 5,000 words shorter across the site, excluding navigation and footers. About went from roughly 890 words to 270, and the pace calculator from roughly 1,200 to 890. The cuts primarily remove repeated introductions, signposting and duplicated qualifications.

Use an ordinary heading when a paragraph needs a label. Save boxes for controls, results and advice a runner needs to notice. Put the number or decision first and explain the assumption once. Use first person for recorded experiences and keep plans clearly identified as plans.

The regression suite covers route and fragment integrity, canonical URLs, calculator maths, share links, downloads, keyboard navigation and printed output. Shared presentation rules apply to screens, so existing print styles continue to govern bands and worksheets.
